title: Client Service Credits for Kiosk Outage and Missed Restocking
content:
The clause reading "Where the kiosk could not take a payment, or the market stood empty because a scheduled restock was missed, the client is credited against the settlement invoice for that period." is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current bases on which a credit against an Unattended Micro Market Program settlement invoice is worked out.

Likewise **no longer in force** is the clause reading "Each hour of kiosk outage inside opening hours earns the percentage of the settlement printed against the market format", superseded by the current basis for a chargeable hour.

## What still governs a credit

The credits allowed in one settlement period are held to the ceiling printed against the market format. Outage is measured from the approved market service requests on the agreement for that period, which the records carry as service credit claims, and not from the client's recollection of when the screen was dark.

Outage caused by the client — a power cut on their floor, a network they took down, a door they locked — is not kiosk outage for this purpose and earns no credit. Where measured availability stayed at or above the uptime guarantee printed against the market format, no credit is allowed however many short interruptions there were. Where the credits that would be due exceed the settlement period ceiling, the ceiling is allowed and the balance of the claim is closed rather than carried forward.

## The claim window

A credit is allowed only when the claim reaches Larkspur Table no later than the claim window for the market format, counted in calendar days from the day the settlement invoice was posted. Claim window days are counted as calendar days from the day after the settlement invoice posting day, every day of the week counts, and a claim arriving on the boundary day itself is still in time; calendar days are never converted into full 24-hour periods.

The posting day is taken from the company's own record of that settlement invoice, matched to the claim by the invoice reference, rather than from the date the client says they received it. The comparison is not-later-than, and equality on the boundary day satisfies it.
